title: Chinese Hand Gestures
synopsis: Hand gestures are different in different countries. Learn more about Chinese hand gestures.

fullText.simplified:
中国的手势

    手势是一种无声的“语言”。很多时候，不用说话，做一个手势，别人就知道意思。每个国家，手势表示的意思都不太一样，今天给大家介绍几个中国的手势。
    觉得别人厉害，特别棒的时候，中国人一般都会竖起右手的大拇指，再加上语言和表情，被夸的人一定会非常高兴的。
    希望愿望成真或者得到上天的帮助，人们会双手合十，放在鼻子和嘴前边，闭着眼说出心中的想法。
    有时候，觉得别人帮了自己一个大忙或者自己有错，得到了别人的原谅，人们会双手合十，放在胸前，轻轻前后摆动，嘴里还会说着“谢谢”。
    长辈招呼年轻人或者小朋友会抬高右手，手心向下，上下摆动。意思就是让对方过来。
    对了，还有一个手势需要告诉大家。有时候，人们会用食指指别人，常常是让别人做事、兴奋、生气等时候会出现这个手势。其实没有什么特别的意思。随着文化交流的增加，现在这个手势变少了，因为越来越多的人发现这样做可能有点不太礼貌。
    生活中的手势还有很多，以后我们慢慢聊。
fullText.traditional:
中國的手勢

    手勢是一種無聲的“語言”。很多時候，不用說話，做一個手勢，別人就知道意思。每個國家，手勢表示的意思都不太一樣，今天給大家介紹幾個中國的手勢。
    覺得別人厲害，特別棒的時候，中國人一般都會豎起右手的大拇指，再加上語言和表情，被誇的人一定會非常高興的。
    希望願望成真或者得到上天的幫助，人們會雙手合十，放在鼻子和嘴前邊，閉著眼說出心中的想法。
    有時候，覺得別人幫了自己一個大忙或者自己有錯，得到了別人的原諒，人們會雙手合十，放在胸前，輕輕前後擺動，嘴裡還會說著“謝謝”。
    長輩招呼年輕人或者小朋友會抬高右手，手心向下，上下擺動。意思就是讓對方過來。
    對了，還有一個手勢需要告訴大家。有時候，人們會用食指指別人，常常是讓別人做事、興奮、生氣等時候會出現這個手勢。其實沒有什麼特別的意思。隨著文化交流的增加，現在這個手勢變少了，因為越來越多的人發現這樣做可能有點不太禮貌。
    生活中的手勢還有很多，以後我們慢慢聊。

sentences.simplified: 手势是一种无声的“语言”。
sentences.traditional: 手勢是一種無聲的“語言”。
sentences.pinyin: shǒu shì shì yì zhǒng wú shēng de yǔ yán

sentences.simplified: 很多时候，不用说话，做一个手势，别人就知道意思。
sentences.traditional: 很多時候，不用說話，做一個手勢，別人就知道意思。
sentences.pinyin: hěn duō shí hou bú yòng shuō huà zuò yí ge shǒu shì bié ren jiù zhī dào yì si
sentences.english: Hand gestures are a type of silent “language”.

sentences.simplified: 每个国家，手势表示的意思都不太一样，今天给大家介绍几个中国的手势。
sentences.traditional: 每個國家，手勢表示的意思都不太一樣，今天給大家介紹幾個中國的手勢。
sentences.pinyin: měi ge guó jiā shǒu shì biǎo shì de yì si dōu bú tài yí yàng jīn tiān gěi dà jiā jiè shào jǐ ge zhōng guó de shǒu shì
sentences.english: A lot of the time, you can simply make a hand gesture, and others will understand what you mean without even having spoken.
Each country has different meanings for different hand gestures. Today, I’d like to introduce some Chinese hand gestures to everyone.

sentences.simplified: 觉得别人厉害，特别棒的时候，中国人一般都会竖起右手的大拇指，
sentences.traditional: 覺得別人厲害，特別棒的時候，中國人一般都會豎起右手的大拇指，
sentences.pinyin: jué de bié ren lì hai tè bié bàng de shí hou zhōng guó rén yì bān dōu huì shù qǐ yòu shǒu de dà mu zhǐ

sentences.simplified: 再加上语言和表情，被夸的人一定会非常高兴的。
sentences.traditional: 再加上語言和表情，被誇的人一定會非常高興的。
sentences.pinyin: zài jiā shàng yǔ yán hé biǎo qíng bèi kuā de rén yí dìng huì fēi cháng gāo xìng de
sentences.english: When Chinese people think someone did a good job on something, they’ll typically give a thumbs up with their right hand.
Add some words and expressions of encouragement, and the person being complimented will for sure be very happy.

sentences.simplified: 希望愿望成真或者得到上天的帮助，
sentences.traditional: 希望願望成真或者得到上天的幫助，
sentences.pinyin: xī wàng yuàn wàng chéng zhēn huò zhě dé dào shàng tiān de bāng zhù

sentences.simplified: 人们会双手合十，放在鼻子和嘴前边，闭着眼说出心中的想法。
sentences.traditional: 人們會雙手合十，放在鼻子和嘴前邊，閉著眼說出心中的想法。
sentences.pinyin: rén men huì shuāng shǒu hé shí fàng zài bí zi hé zuǐ qián bian bì zhe yǎn shuō chū xīn zhōng de xiǎng fǎ
sentences.english: When people want a wish to come true or when they want some help from above, ..
.. they will put their palms together in front of their nose and mouth, close their eyes, and voice what’s in their heart.

sentences.simplified: 有时候，觉得别人帮了自己一个大忙或者自己有错，得到了别人的原谅，
sentences.traditional: 有時候，覺得別人幫了自己一個大忙或者自己有錯，得到了別人的原諒，
sentences.pinyin: yǒu shí hou jué de bié ren bāng le zì jǐ yí ge dà máng huò zhě zì jǐ yǒu cuò dé dào le bié ren de yuán liàng

sentences.simplified: 人们会双手合十，放在胸前，轻轻前后摆动，嘴里还会说着“谢谢”。
sentences.traditional: 人們會雙手合十，放在胸前，輕輕前後擺動，嘴裡還會說著“謝謝”。
sentences.pinyin: rén men huì shuāng shǒu hé shí fàng zài xiōng qián qīng qīng qián hòu bǎi dòng zuǐ lǐ hái huì shuō zhe xiè xie
sentences.english: Sometimes, when people feel that someone has done them a great favor, or when they feel that they have been forgiven for a mistake ..
.. they will put their palms together in front of their chest and rock their hands back and forth, all while saying “thank you”.

sentences.simplified: 长辈招呼年轻人或者小朋友会抬高右手，手心向下，上下摆动。
sentences.traditional: 長輩招呼年輕人或者小朋友會抬高右手，手心向下，上下擺動。
sentences.pinyin: zhǎng bèi zhāo hu nián qīng rén huò zhě xiǎo péng you huì tái gāo yòu shǒu shǒu xīn xiàng xià shàng xià bǎi dòng

sentences.simplified: 意思就是让对方过来。
sentences.traditional: 意思就是讓對方過來。
sentences.pinyin: yì si jiù shì ràng duì fāng guò lái
sentences.english: When elders want to call over younger people or children, they will raise their right arm palm down, and wave up and down.
It means they want the person to come over to where they are.

sentences.simplified: 对了，还有一个手势需要告诉大家。
sentences.traditional: 對了，還有一個手勢需要告訴大家。
sentences.pinyin: duì le hái yǒu yí ge shǒu shì xū yào gào su dà jiā

sentences.simplified: 有时候，人们会用食指指别人，
sentences.traditional: 有時候，人們會用食指指別人，
sentences.pinyin: yǒu shí hou rén men huì yòng shí zhǐ zhǐ bié ren
sentences.english: Oh right, there’s another hand gesture that I wanted to tell everyone about.

sentences.simplified: 常常是让别人做事、兴奋、生气等时候会出现这个手势。
sentences.traditional: 常常是讓別人做事、興奮、生氣等時候會出現這個手勢。
sentences.pinyin: cháng cháng shì ràng bié ren zuò shì xīng fèn shēng qì děng shí hou huì chū xiàn zhè ge shǒu shì
sentences.english: Sometimes, people will use their index finger to point at others.

sentences.simplified: 其实没有什么特别的意思。
sentences.traditional: 其實沒有什麼特別的意思。
sentences.pinyin: qí shí méi yǒu shén me tè bié de yì si
sentences.english: This gesture often appears when people ask others to do something, when they get excited or angry, etc.

sentences.simplified: 随着文化交流的增加，现在这个手势变少了，
sentences.traditional: 隨著文化交流的增加，現在這個手勢變少了，
sentences.pinyin: suí zhe wén huà jiāo liú de zēng jiā xiàn zài zhè ge shǒu shì biàn shǎo le
sentences.english: But, there is actually no particular meaning to this gesture.

sentences.simplified: 因为越来越多的人发现这样做可能有点不太礼貌。
sentences.traditional: 因為越來越多的人發現這樣做可能有點不太禮貌。
sentences.pinyin: yīn wèi yuè lái yuè duō de rén fā xiàn zhè yàng zuò kě néng yǒu diǎn bú tài lǐ mào
sentences.english: With the increase of cultural exchange, this gesture has been used less frequently.
This is because more and more people have begun to find it a little impolite.

sentences.simplified: 生活中的手势还有很多，以后我们慢慢聊。
sentences.traditional: 生活中的手勢還有很多，以後我們慢慢聊。
sentences.pinyin: shēng huó zhōng de shǒu shì hái yǒu hěn duō yǐ hòu wǒ men màn man liáo

sentences.english: There are a lot of other hand gestures commonly used in life – we’ll talk more next time.

raw.synopsis: Hand gestures are different in different countries. Learn more about Chinese hand gestures.
sentence_translations: Hand gestures are a type of silent “language”.
A lot of the time, you can simply make a hand gesture, and others will understand what you mean without even having spoken.
Each country has different meanings for different hand gestures. Today, I’d like to introduce some Chinese hand gestures to everyone.
When Chinese people think someone did a good job on something, they’ll typically give a thumbs up with their right hand.
Add some words and expressions of encouragement, and the person being complimented will for sure be very happy.
When people want a wish to come true or when they want some help from above, ..
.. they will put their palms together in front of their nose and mouth, close their eyes, and voice what’s in their heart.
Sometimes, when people feel that someone has done them a great favor, or when they feel that they have been forgiven for a mistake ..
.. they will put their palms together in front of their chest and rock their hands back and forth, all while saying “thank you”.
When elders want to call over younger people or children, they will raise their right arm palm down, and wave up and down.
It means they want the person to come over to where they are.
Oh right, there’s another hand gesture that I wanted to tell everyone about.
Sometimes, people will use their index finger to point at others.
This gesture often appears when people ask others to do something, when they get excited or angry, etc.
But, there is actually no particular meaning to this gesture.
With the increase of cultural exchange, this gesture has been used less frequently.
This is because more and more people have begun to find it a little impolite.
There are a lot of other hand gestures commonly used in life – we’ll talk more next time.
